title: Diagnostic relevance of myosonography in hereditary myopathies
summary:
Muscle ultrasound has become increasingly important in the diagnosis of neuromuscular diseases in recent years.  However, further studies are needed to assess the added diagnostic value in terms of a correlation with disease severity and clinical limitations of patients, as well as to differentiate between the various myopathies using myosonography.  
As part of the study, a comprehensive myosonographic examination of patients with hereditary muscle diseases is to be carried out. 
Functional tests such as hand strength measurement, muscle strength testing and gait testing are also carried out to record the patient's clinical disability. 
In addition, the diagnosis and disease key data, such as the duration and severity of the physical limitations as well as the secondary diagnoses are recorded.

The aim of this study is, on the one hand, to show the disease-specific differences in myosonography between different hereditary myopathies in order to support differential diagnosis between the diseases and, on the other hand, to determine the diagnostic significance of myosonography as a prognostic marker with regard to the clinical functional limitations of the patients.
